lesson_title: Finance Essentials: The Hole, the Shovel and the Count
hook_text: A boerewors stand loses money on its first 119 sales of the month. Sale 120 changes everything.
clip_script: The corner site costs R1 800 whether he grills or sleeps. That is the hole the month starts in. Each roll sells for R31 but eats R16 of ingredients — so each sale throws R15 into the hole. The only question that matters in week one: how many R15 shovelfuls fill a R1 800 hole? 1 800 over 15 — 120. Roll number 120 lands exactly at ground level: income R3 720, costs R3 720, nothing lost, nothing gained. Roll 121 is the first one he actually profits from — R15 clean. Every break-even question is these three numbers in costume: the hole, the shovel, the count. Car washes, tuck shops, salon chairs — same three numbers, every time.
visual_style: A literal hole labelled R1 800 filling with golden R15 coins one boerewors roll at a time, a counter racing to 120, then the ground level breaking into green profit territory at 121.
pacing: Slow reveal of the hole, accelerating coin montage, sharp freeze on sale 120, triumphant beat at 121.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson to master every money move before your final exams.
